item.title: Orbital Marine Power Secures New UK Contract and Expands Global Pipeline
item.description: Orbital Marine Power has secured a new UK Contract for Difference award, expanding its project portfolio to 17MW and strengthening its global tidal energy pipeline across the UK and Canada.The post Orbital Marine Power Secures New UK Contract and Expands Global Pipeline appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Orbex Releases Unseen Prime Images as Administration Looms
item.description: Orbex has released unseen images of its Prime microlauncher in near flight configuration as the company prepares to enter administration, highlighting the progress made ahead of planned UK test launches.The post Orbex Releases Unseen Prime Images as Administration Looms appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Angus MacNeil Named as ALBA Highlands and Islands Lead Candidate
item.description: Angus Brendan MacNeil has been confirmed as ALBA’s lead candidate for the Highlands and Islands Regional List, setting out his party’s strategy ahead of the next Scottish Parliament election.The post Angus MacNeil Named as ALBA Highlands and Islands Lead Candidate appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Deborah Meaden Urges Public to Back Mary’s Meals on Random Acts of Kindness Day
item.description: Deborah Meaden is urging people to support Mary’s Meals ahead of Random Acts of Kindness Day, highlighting how 10p can help feed hungry children and support more than three million pupils worldwide.The post Deborah Meaden Urges Public to Back Mary’s Meals on Random Acts of Kindness Day appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: UNITED Campaign Shines Light on Football’s Community Impact
item.description: The SPFL, SWPL and SPFL Trust have launched the UNITED: Football in the Community campaign, celebrating the work of 46 community trusts supporting health, education and inclusion across Scotland.The post UNITED Campaign Shines Light on Football’s Community Impact appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Cobbs Reappointed to Run Port of Cromarty Firth Gift Shop
item.description: Cobbs has been re appointed to run the Port of Cromarty Firth gift shop in Invergordon for the 2026 and 2027 cruise seasons, as more than 95 ships prepare to visit the Highland port this year.The post Cobbs Reappointed to Run Port of Cromarty Firth Gift Shop appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Aberdeen Scientists Launch World First Brain Health Study Using Next Generation Imaging
item.description: Scientists at the University of Aberdeen have launched a world first brain health study using next generation Field Cycling Imaging technology to detect early signs of cerebral small vessel disease linked to stroke and dementia.The post Aberdeen Scientists Launch World First Brain Health Study Using Next Generation Imaging appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Eastgate Displays Highlight Hidden Mental Health Struggles in Inverness
item.description: Mental health charity Centred Scotland has installed three powerful displays at Inverness’s Eastgate Centre, highlighting hidden mental ill health and promoting its free Discovery College walk in support service.The post Eastgate Displays Highlight Hidden Mental Health Struggles in Inverness appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Western Isles EV Drivers Told to Prepare for Charger Network Switch
item.description: EV drivers in the Western Isles are being urged to prepare for a public charger network switch from ChargePlace Scotland to ScottishPower in early March, with new apps and RFID cards required.The post Western Isles EV Drivers Told to Prepare for Charger Network Switch appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: SNP Criticises Labour Over £63 Million Election Cost
item.description: The SNP has criticised the UK Government after it confirmed a £63 million cost linked to a legal U turn over council elections in England, claiming Scottish families should not foot the bill.The post SNP Criticises Labour Over £63 Million Election Cost appeared first on The Highland Times.
